transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess… what brought me in is some evenings after work, especially if I’ve been really strict with myself all day, I kind of lose the thread. I’ll eat dinner, and then it turns into cereal, crackers, leftovers, something sweet—just a lot more than I meant to, all within a couple hours.  

And I mean, work has been busy too, insurance stuff never really stops, people call at the worst times—but yeah, the eating in the evenings is why I’m here.
After these episodes of eating more than you intended, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, using laxatives, exercising a lot more than usual, or anything like that?

I don’t really make myself sick or anything like that. But… the next day, I’ll get it in my head that I have to make up for it. Like I’ll skip breakfast, then lunch too, and tell myself I’m just “getting back on track.”

Or I’ll go for a much longer hike than I normally would, or push harder at softball conditioning even if I’m tired. Which is silly because then I’m dragging at work the next day, and with insurance calls you really can’t be half-awake—people notice if you miss one little detail. But yeah, it’s more that kind of thing, trying to balance it out afterward.
When you find yourself eating more than you intended in the evening, does it ever feel like you can’t stop yourself or control what you’re eating, even if you wanted to?

Yeah… that’s probably the part that scares me a little. Once I get started on those nights, I keep going back to the kitchen even while I’m telling myself, “Okay, stop now, that’s enough.”

It’s not even always that I’m enjoying it by then. It’s like I’m just… on autopilot. I’ll open the cabinet, close it, then a few minutes later I’m back there again. And I don’t really feel like I’m back in charge until I’m uncomfortably full. Then I kind of snap out of it and think, “Why did I do that?”
Do these evening eating episodes cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your daily life in any way?

It does upset me, yeah. I mean, I’m not falling apart or anything—I still get to work, keep up with my clients, and I help mentor some of the newer people at the office. And at home, I still do what needs doing.

But it kind of gets in my head. Like if I have some public thing coming up, or a work event where I have to look put together, I’ll start worrying about how my clothes fit. Then I’m distracted and not as confident as I usually would be. Which is frustrating, because I’ve been doing insurance sales long enough to know how to talk to people, you know? I shouldn’t be thinking about my waistband when I’m supposed to be listening to someone.
How often do these evening eating episodes happen—like, how many nights a week would you say this occurs?

Most weeks, I’d say. Not every single night or anything… usually maybe one or two nights in a week where I eat way more than I meant to.

It’s been like that for the past few months, I guess. Sometimes it lines up with stressful workdays—though honestly, in insurance, there’s always some call or paperwork issue, so I don’t know if that’s even a useful measure. But yeah, generally one or two evenings, and then the next day I’m doing that whole “make up for it” thing, like skipping meals or taking a longer walk than I normally would.

Can you describe what goes through your mind right before one of these evening eating episodes starts? Do you feel like you have control over what you’re doing, or does it feel like something you can’t stop even if you want to?

Usually right before it starts, I’m thinking I’ll just have a little something, like it’s no big deal. And then once I’m in the kitchen… I don’t know, it kind of turns into this loop.

I’ll tell myself, “Stop, you’ve had enough,” but then I’m back opening the fridge or the cabinet again. It reminds me a little of when I’m at work and I keep checking the same file because I feel like I missed something—except this is with food, and it feels worse because it’s my own kitchen and I should be able to just walk away.

So no, I don’t really feel in control once it gets going. I don’t feel like I’m back in charge until I’m way too full, like uncomfortable. Then I sort of snap out of it and feel upset with myself.
During these evening eating episodes, would you say that you feel a complete lack of control over your eating—like you’re not able to stop or control how much you eat once you start?

Yeah… I think that’s fair to say. Once I get started on those nights, it’s like I keep circling back to the kitchen even while I’m literally telling myself, “Just stop now.”

It’s strange, because in other parts of my life I’m pretty controlled—like at work, I can keep track of clients and policies and all that—but with this, in the moment, I don’t feel like I’m really in charge. I don’t feel like I’ve got a handle on it again until I’m already uncomfortably full.
Would you say these evening eating episodes cause you a lot of distress or affect how well you can function in your daily life, like at work or socially?

It bothers me, yeah. I wouldn’t say I’m falling apart or anything—I’m still getting to work, keeping up with my clients, and I still do the mentoring stuff they’ve asked me to do. At home I’m managing what I need to manage too.

But it gets in my head. Like if I know I have to go to some public event or meet people face-to-face, I’ll start worrying about how my clothes fit, and then I feel distracted and not as confident. Which is silly, because half the time nobody’s even noticing, they’re just worried about their own paperwork or whatever… but it still makes me feel off.
During these evening eating episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than normal?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really timed myself or thought about the speed of it. I know I’m sort of… distracted and going back and forth, opening things, taking bites, but whether it’s faster than normal, I don’t know.

Sometimes I feel rushed in my head, if that makes sense, like when I’m trying to get out the door for a client meeting and suddenly can’t find my keys, but I don’t know if I’m actually eating rapidly. I’d have to pay attention to that more.
During these evening eating episodes, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yes… I do. Not every single time, maybe, but on those nights when it gets going, I’ll keep going back to the kitchen even while I’m telling myself, okay, enough, stop now.

And then it’s like I don’t really feel like I’m back in control until I’m already too full—like uncomfortable full. Which is frustrating, because I’ll think, why didn’t I just stop twenty minutes ago? It’s like when I keep checking the same paperwork at work even though I know it’s done, except this feels worse because it’s my body, you know?
Do you find yourself eating large amounts of food during these evening episodes even when you’re not actually hungry?

Yeah… yes, that happens. It’s usually in the evening after work, especially if I’ve been trying to be “good” all day, you know, keeping things very strict. Then I’ll come home and I’m not even sure I’m really hungry anymore, but I start with dinner, and then somehow it’s cereal, crackers, whatever leftovers are there, maybe something sweet… all within a couple hours.

And then I’m standing there thinking, why did I do all that? It’s not like when I was younger and my kids were home and everyone was grazing in the kitchen—well, they’re grown now, but you know what I mean. It’s more like I just meant to have one thing, and it turns into way more than I planned.
Do you ever find yourself eating these larger amounts of food in secret because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

I don’t really know how to answer that. I mean, I’m usually home in the evening, so it’s not like I’m at a restaurant with people watching me or anything. My kids are grown and not around the kitchen like they used to be, so a lot of the time I’m just by myself anyway.

I guess I don’t think of it as “secret,” exactly… but I also don’t exactly want anyone seeing it. Like if someone called or came by, I’d probably straighten up the kitchen first, you know? But then again, I do that with paperwork on the counter too, so I don’t know if that counts as embarrassment or just me not wanting people in my business.

And then I’m standing there thinking, why did I do all that? It’s not like when I was younger and my kids were home and everyone was grazing in the kitchen—well, they’re grown now, but you know what I mean. It’s more like I just meant to have one thing, and it turns into way more than I planned.
